name: NetWatcher
description: NetWatcher monitors UniFi Network for unknown devices, stores history in SQLite, and sends pluggable alerts. Native Debian LXC install with uv-managed Python 3.14, systemd hardening, and safe in-place upgrades.

notes.text: Change the bootstrap Web UI password (admin/admin) immediately under Security after first login.
NetWatcher starts in UniFi mock mode. Edit /etc/netwatcher/netwatcher.env with your UniFi URL and dedicated account, set UNIFI_MOCK_MODE=false, then run: systemctl restart netwatcher

Persistent data lives in /var/lib/netwatcher (SQLite DB + app-secret.key). Configuration is /etc/netwatcher/netwatcher.env. Always back up the database and app-secret.key together — restoring only the DB without the matching key makes encrypted notification settings unreadable.

Trusted-host checks are enabled by default. Access via http://<container-ip>:8080 initially (private/loopback IP literals). Add DNS names under Security → Trusted Hosts. Prefer an HTTPS reverse proxy; do not expose NetWatcher directly to the public internet.
Update by re-running the Community Script inside the LXC. Updates preserve configuration, database, and encryption key, and roll back automatically on failure.
Logs: journalctl -u netwatcher -f — Status: systemctl status netwatcher
